title: g-pichler/bsc-averaging
abstract:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib development that settles three previously open problems about
binary channels on a doubly symmetric binary source (DSBS): a pair (X, Y) of Bernoulli(1/2)
bits with P(X != Y) = p, together with Markov chains U - X - Y - V in which U and V are the
outputs of two independent binary channels applied to X and to Y. All quantities are in nats.

(1) MathOverflow 285151, "Do averaged binary symmetric channels maximize mutual information?"
(Georg Pichler, 2017; unanswered there) asks whether conv A = conv B, where A is the set of
rate triples (R0, R1, R2) with I(U;X) <= R1, I(Y;V) <= R2 and R0 <= I(U;V) attainable by
arbitrary binary channels on the two sides, and B is the same set with both channels
restricted to be binary symmetric. The inclusion B subset A is elementary; the question is
whether taking convex hulls closes the gap, which the counterexample to the predecessor
question MathOverflow 213084 leaves open. This development proves conv A = conv B for every
p in [0,1] (`averaged_bsc_maximise_mutual_information`). The same statement settles
Conjecture 5.2 of Pichler, Piantanida and Matz, "Distributed Information-Theoretic
Clustering", Information and Inference 11 (2022) 1029-1082.

(2), (3) Conjectures 1 and 2 of Dikshtein, Ordentlich and Shamai (Shitz), "The Double-Sided
Information Bottleneck Function", Entropy 24(9):1321 (2022), which concern the double-sided
information bottleneck function R(Cu, Cv) = max I(U;V) subject to I(X;U) <= Cu and
I(Y;V) <= Cv at p = 0, that is X = Y. Conjecture 1 predicts that the maximising test channels
are a Z-channel and an S-channel; Conjecture 2 predicts that the pair maximising I(X;U,V) are
both Z-channels. Both are proved here for binary U and V, in optimality form: the Challenge
statements exhibit the conjectured channels themselves as `Chan` values and say that no
admissible pair beats them. No admissible pair exceeds the I(U;V) of the Z/S pair
(`conjecture1_p0_holds`), and none undercuts that of the Z/Z pair (`conjecture2_p0_holds`), at
every nondegenerate rate pair. A Z-channel and an S-channel are the same transition matrix up
to relabelling the input alphabet, so what the two conjectures distinguish is the relative
orientation of the two sides: anti-aligned for the maximum, aligned for the minimum.

The development is sorry-free and contains no hand-written axiom declaration.
`averaged_bsc_maximise_mutual_information` and `conjecture2_p0_holds` depend only on `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. `conjecture1_p0_holds` additionally depends on exactly one
further axiom: the 24129-monomial Polya certificate of its kernel lemma is checked by
`native_decide`, which on Lean v4.32.0 mints a per-declaration auxiliary axiom
(BSCAveraging.Reflect.kerQPE_allNonneg._native.native_decide.ax_1_1) rather than citing
`Lean.ofReduceBool`; that auxiliary axiom is a custom axiom in Comparator's sense. The other
computed step of that proof, a 650-cell interval sweep, is checked by the Lean kernel and adds
no axiom.

Scope, stated once for all three results. The channels are binary on both sides. For (1) this
is the setting of the source question. For (2) and (3) the reduction of the double-sided
bottleneck over arbitrary alphabets to binary test channels is Proposition 3 of the
Dikshtein-Ordentlich-Shamai paper and Proposition 4.3 of the Pichler-Piantanida-Matz paper; it
is cited here, not formalized, so read as statements about R(Cu, Cv, 0) with unrestricted
alphabets, (2) and (3) are conditional on that published cardinality bound. Conjecture 2 is
stated in its minimisation form, min I(U;V) at fixed rates; the identity
I(U;V) = I(U;X) + I(V;X) - I(X;U,V) that turns the paper's maximisation of I(X;U,V) into
that minimisation is the authors' own, given as Remark 5 of the same paper, and is likewise
not formalized here. Both
conjecture statements are value statements: they say the conjectured optimal value is not
beaten, not that the conjectured pair is the unique optimiser. p = 0 is the only case the
paper's Conjectures 1 and 2 state; Conjecture 3 of that paper, which concerns p above a
threshold, is not addressed.

Two endpoints of (1) were already settled in the literature and are reproved here rather than
established: p = 0, which Pichler-Piantanida-Matz note follows from their Corollary 4.1 and
Proposition 4.3, and the degenerate p = 1/2, where the two regions coincide without
convexification. The new content of (1) is p in (0,1/2) union (1/2,1). The binary restriction
costs nothing in (1): Conjecture 5.2 is stated for S_i, which is defined with the cardinality
bounds |U| <= |X| and |V| <= |Y|, and Proposition 4.3 of the same paper gives
conv(S_i) = conv(R_i).

Novelty has not been independently established. MathOverflow 285151 has no answer and no
comments (StackExchange API, asked 2017-11-03). The Dikshtein-Ordentlich-Shamai paper has one
recorded citing work, a 2024 Entropy editorial that mentions the setting but not the
conjectures, and no resolution of either conjecture was found. Mathlib at the pinned revision
contains no mutual information at all, and no prior Lean formalization of any of the three
problems was found. That search is the authors' own and is not offered as evidence of
priority.
